Issue #187: GoThru SSO Logout API Implementation

Scope

Villume exposes two public logout endpoints backed by the GoThru Keycloak OIDC logout and revoke flows:

  1. POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout (Primary / Recommended endpoint for GoThru SSO)
  2. POST /v1/auth/logout (Generic alias, useful if frontend uses a generic auth service)

Both endpoints utilize the same underlying handler (GoThruLogout) to:

  • Terminate the active user session in Keycloak (so that subsequent SSO logins require credentials instead of automatically logging back in).
  • Revoke associated Keycloak tokens.

Configuration (Backend)

KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_URL=https://gothru-sso.web.id
KEYCLOAK_REALM=gothru
KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE=villume-dev
  • KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL is preferred. KEYCLOAK_URL is used as a fallback.
  • KEYCLOAK_REALM defaults to gothru.
  • KEYCLOAK_AUDIENCE is directly used as the Keycloak client ID (villume-dev). No new environment variables are required.

Frontend Integration Guide

1. Endpoint Reference

Endpoint Method Auth Header Description
/v1/auth/gothru/logout POST Optional (Public) Primary endpoint for GoThru SSO logout.
/v1/auth/logout POST Optional (Public) Generic alias for logout.

Note: Both endpoints are registered under AuthJWTExclude. The frontend can call them even if the Villume session JWT has already expired in the browser.

2. Request Payloads

Option A: Send refresh_token (Recommended)

Send the Keycloak refresh_token stored in the frontend upon login.

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option B: Send both refresh_token and access_token

If the frontend stores both, the API will terminate the Keycloak session using refresh_token and revoke the access_token simultaneously.

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option C: Compatibility Alias token

If the frontend stores only a single token variable:

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}

Option D: Authorization Header Fallback

If the request body is empty, the API also extracts the token from the Authorization header:

POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout
Authorization: Bearer <keycloak-refresh-token>

3. Response Reference

Success (200 OK)

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "messages": "Logout success",
    "code": "success"
  }
}

Error: Missing Token (400 Bad Request)

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "BAD_REQUEST",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Required GoThru refresh token"
    }
  }
}

Error: Malformed JSON (400 Bad Request)

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "data": {
    "status": "BAD_REQUEST",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Invalid request body"
    }
  }
}

Error: Expired or Rejected Keycloak Token (401 Unauthorized)

{
  "statusCode": 401,
  "data": {
    "status": "UNAUTHORIZED",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Unauthorized or expired GoThru token"
    }
  }
}

Error: Keycloak Unreachable or Provider Failure (502 Bad Gateway)

{
  "statusCode": 502,
  "data": {
    "status": "BAD_GATEWAY",
    "valid": false,
    "errors": {
      "messages": "Cannot process GoThru logout"
    }
  }
}

4. Frontend Code Examples

A. Using fetch (TypeScript / JavaScript)

interface LogoutResponse {
  statusCode: number;
  data: {
    valid: boolean;
    messages: string;
    code?: string;
  };
}

async function logoutGoThru(): Promise<void> {
  const refreshToken = localStorage.getItem('gothru_refresh_token');

  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/v1/auth/gothru/logout`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        refresh_token: refreshToken,
      }),
    });

    const result: LogoutResponse = await res.json();
    console.log('Logout response:', result.data.messages);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Logout error:', error);
  } finally {
    // Always clear client-side auth tokens regardless of response
    localStorage.removeItem('token'); // Villume session JWT
    localStorage.removeItem('gothru_access_token');
    localStorage.removeItem('gothru_refresh_token');

    // Redirect user to the login page
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }
}

B. Using axios

import axios from 'axios';

async function handleLogout(): Promise<void> {
  const refreshToken = localStorage.getItem('gothru_refresh_token');

  try {
    await axios.post('/v1/auth/gothru/logout', {
      refresh_token: refreshToken,
    });
  } catch (err) {
    // If 401 (token already expired / invalidated in Keycloak), continue local cleanup
    console.warn('Keycloak session already expired or invalidated');
  } finally {
    localStorage.clear();
    sessionStorage.clear();
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }
}

Logout Flow & Sequence

  1. Frontend Request: The client calls POST /v1/auth/gothru/logout passing refresh_token.
  2. Token Validation: Villume validates the presence of a token. If none is found, returns 400 Bad Request.
  3. Keycloak OIDC Session Termination:
    • Villume sends POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/logout to Keycloak with client_id=villume-dev and refresh_token.
    • Keycloak invalidates the user session across the SSO Realm.
  4. Token Revocation (Optional):
    • If an access_token was also included, Villume calls /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/revoke to invalidate the access token.
  5. Success Response: Villume returns { statusCode: 200, data: { valid: true, messages: "Logout success", code: "success" } }.
  6. Frontend Cleanup: The frontend removes stored session tokens (token, gothru_refresh_token, etc.) and redirects the user to the login screen.

Implementation Files

  • src/action/v1/auth/keycloakService.go: Keycloak HTTP client service (VerifyAccessToken, Logout, RevokeToken)
  • src/action/v1/auth/authKeycloakLogout.go: Logout handler action (GoThruLogout)
  • src/action/v1/auth/keycloakService_test.go: Unit tests for KeycloakService
  • src/action/v1/auth/authKeycloakLogout_test.go: Unit and integration tests for HTTP handler
  • src/controllers/v1/authController.go: Controller entry point (GoThruLogout)
  • src/routes/v1/authRoutes.go: Route registration for /v1/auth/gothru/logout and /v1/auth/logout
  • src/routes/v1/route.go: Public route exclusion in AuthJWTExclude
  • api-collection/Villume GO/Auth/GoThru Logout.yml: Bruno HTTP request with token clear script
  • api-collection/Villume GO/environments/*.yml: Environment variable gothru_refresh_token

Verification

go test ./...
go vet ./...

Keycloak API Reference & Developer Tutorial Guide

This guide provides a comprehensive reference and hands-on tutorial for interacting with the GoThru SSO Keycloak APIs. It covers standard OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0 endpoints for authentication/authorization and the Keycloak Admin REST API for managing users, credentials, roles, and clients.

Table of Contents

    • 2.2 Service Account Token (Client Credentials Grant)

1. Environment & Endpoints Overview

Keycloak exposes two main categories of APIs:

  1. OIDC / OAuth 2.0 Endpoints: Mounted at /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/*. Used by frontend clients, mobile apps, and backend APIs for login, token issuance, user verification, and token exchange.
  2. Admin REST API: Mounted at /admin/realms/{realm}/*. Used by backend services, CI/CD, migration scripts, and administrative systems to manage users, groups, roles, and clients.

Configured Realms

Realm Description
master Primary administrative realm used to authenticate admin users and obtain admin management tokens.
gothru GoThru application realm containing all users, federations, clients (e.g. panorra-app, testingin), and roles.

Base URLs by Environment

Environment Base URL Realm Admin Console
Local Dev http://127.0.0.1:8180 gothru http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin
Dev Server https://gothru-sso.web.id gothru https://gothru-sso.web.id/admin
Production https://auth.gothru.co (or https://id.gothru.org) gothru https://auth.gothru.co/admin

2. Authentication & Token Acquisition

2.1 Admin CLI Token (Password Grant)

Used by admin scripts, migration tooling, and CLI tasks to obtain a bearer token for the Admin REST API.

Endpoint:
POST /realms/{admin_realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "client_id=admin-cli" \
  -d "grant_type=password" \
  -d "username=admin" \
  -d "password=your_admin_password"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "expires_in": 60,
  "refresh_expires_in": 1800,
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "not-before-policy": 0,
  "session_state": "b3e0c034-7164-4e38-9e6e-2144c8c73499",
  "scope": "profile email"
}

Note

Admin access tokens usually have a short lifetime (e.g., 60 seconds). For long-running batch jobs, refresh the token periodically using the refresh_token or re-authenticate.

2.2 Service Account Token (Client Credentials Grant)

Used for secure machine-to-machine (M2M) communication without a user context. The client must be configured with Client Authentication: ON and Service Accounts Roles: Enabled in Keycloak.

Endpoint:
POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  -d "client_id=backend-service" \
  -d "client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "not-before-policy": 0,
  "scope": "email profile"
}

2.3 User Token (Authorization Code Flow with PKCE)

Used for Single Page Apps (SPA like Panorra PWA) and mobile clients.

Step 1: Generate PKCE Code Verifier & Challenge

  1. Generate high-entropy cryptographic random string (code_verifier).
  2. Calculate SHA-256 hash of code_verifier and Base64URL-encode it (code_challenge).

Step 2: Redirect User to Keycloak Login

Direct browser to:

https://gothru-sso.web.id/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/auth?
  client_id=panorra-pwa&
  response_type=code&
  scope=openid%20profile%20email&
  redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.panorra.com%2Fcallback&
  state=xyz123random&
  code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrGMTJguCH5rtG6j3DwYZETb_6ecd80&
  code_challenge_method=S256

Step 3: Exchange Authorization Code for Tokens

Once redirected back to redirect_uri?code=AUTH_CODE&state=xyz123random, exchange code via POST:

curl -X POST "https://gothru-sso.web.id/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=authorization_code" \
  -d "client_id=panorra-pwa" \
  -d "code=AUTH_CODE" \
  -d "redirect_uri=https://app.panorra.com/callback" \
  -d "code_verifier=ORIGINAL_CODE_VERIFIER"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...",
  "expires_in": 300,
  "refresh_expires_in": 1800,
  "refresh_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "id_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...",
  "not-before-policy": 0,
  "session_state": "4020ca25-4c07-42c2-843e-cf9a76bc0a31",
  "scope": "openid profile email"
}

2.4 Refreshing an Access Token

Endpoint:
POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=refresh_token" \
  -d "client_id=panorra-pwa" \
  -d "refresh_token=YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"

2.5 Revoking Tokens & Logout

Revoke a Specific Token

Endpoint: POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/revoke

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/revoke" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "client_id=panorra-pwa" \
  -d "token=YOUR_ACCESS_OR_REFRESH_TOKEN" \
  -d "token_type_hint=refresh_token"

End Keycloak User Session (Logout)

Endpoint: POST /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/logout

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/logout" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "client_id=panorra-pwa" \
  -d "refresh_token=YOUR_REFRESH_TOKEN"

3. OpenID Connect (OIDC) Endpoints Reference

3.1 OpenID Configuration Discovery

Used by OIDC client libraries to automatically discover all endpoint URLs, JWKS URIs, supported scopes, and claims.

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/.well-known/openid-configuration
  • Authentication: None (Public)

Example

curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/.well-known/openid-configuration" | jq .

Key Response Fields

{
  "issuer": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru",
  "authorization_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/auth",
  "token_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo",
  "end_session_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/logout",
  "jwks_uri": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/certs",
  "introspection_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token/introspect",
  "revocation_endpoint": "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/revoke"
}

3.2 Authorization Endpoint

Browser redirect endpoint for initiating user login.

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth
  • Query Parameters:
    • client_id (string, required): Client ID configured in Keycloak.
    • response_type (string, required): code.
    • scope (string, required): openid profile email.
    • redirect_uri (string, required): Whitelisted redirect URI.
    • state (string, required): CSRF protection token.
    • code_challenge (string, recommended): Base64URL SHA-256 hash of verifier.
    • code_challenge_method (string, recommended): S256.
    • prompt (string, optional): none, login, consent, select_account.
    • kc_idp_hint (string, optional): Bypass login and redirect directly to identity provider (e.g. google).

3.3 Token Endpoint

Direct HTTP POST endpoint to exchange authorization codes, refresh tokens, client credentials, or user passwords.

  • Method: POST
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token
  • Headers: Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
  • Payload Parameters:
    • grant_type: authorization_code | refresh_token | client_credentials | password
    • client_id: Client identifier
    • client_secret: Required if client authentication is enabled
    • code: Required for grant_type=authorization_code
    • redirect_uri: Required for grant_type=authorization_code
    • code_verifier: Required if PKCE was used
    • refresh_token: Required for grant_type=refresh_token

3.4 UserInfo Endpoint

Returns identity attributes of the authenticated user.

  • Method: GET or POST
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo
  • Headers:
    • Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
    • Accept: application/json

cURL Request

curl -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "sub": "399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d",
  "email_verified": true,
  "name": "John Doe",
  "preferred_username": "johndoe",
  "given_name": "John",
  "family_name": "Doe",
  "email": "johndoe@example.com"
}

3.5 JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) Endpoint

Public cryptographic keys used by backend microservices to verify Keycloak JWT signatures locally without making an HTTP request per API call.

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/certs
  • Authentication: Public

Response (200 OK)

{
  "keys": [
    {
      "kid": "abc123KeyId",
      "kty": "RSA",
      "alg": "RS256",
      "use": "sig",
      "n": "u1wK...",
      "e": "AQAB"
    }
  ]
}

3.6 Token Introspection Endpoint

Allows resource servers / backends to query the active status and metadata of a token.

  • Method: POST
  • Path: /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token/introspect
  • Authentication: Requires client credentials

cURL Request

curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/realms/gothru/protocol/openid-connect/token/introspect" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -u "backend-service:YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -d "token=TOKEN_TO_INSPECT"

Response (200 OK)

{
  "active": true,
  "scope": "openid profile email",
  "client_id": "panorra-pwa",
  "username": "johndoe",
  "exp": 1773289000,
  "sub": "399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d"
}

4. Keycloak Admin REST API Reference

All Admin REST API requests must include:

  • Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_ACCESS_TOKEN>
  • Content-Type: application/json (for POST/PUT requests)
  • Accept: application/json

Base URI: /admin/realms/{realm} (e.g. /admin/realms/gothru)

4.1 User Management

Create User

  • Method: POST
  • Path: /admin/realms/{realm}/users
  • Success Status: 201 Created
  • Note: The user UUID is returned in the HTTP Location response header: .../users/{id}.
Request Payload
{
  "username": "johndoe",
  "email": "johndoe@example.com",
  "firstName": "John",
  "lastName": "Doe",
  "enabled": true,
  "emailVerified": true,
  "attributes": {
    "local_user_id": ["1054"],
    "country": ["US"],
    "legacy_google_id": [""],
    "local_user_type": ["photographer"]
  },
  "credentials": [
    {
      "type": "password",
      "value": "InitialTemporaryPassword123!",
      "temporary": false
    }
  ]
}
cURL Request
curl -i -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin/realms/gothru/users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "username": "johndoe",
    "email": "johndoe@example.com",
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "enabled": true,
    "emailVerified": true,
    "attributes": {
      "local_user_id": ["1054"]
    }
  }'

Search & List Users

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /admin/realms/{realm}/users
  • Query Parameters:
    • search (string): Filter by substring in username, email, firstName, lastName.
    • username (string): Exact or prefix match on username.
    • email (string): Filter by email.
    • exact (bool): true for exact matching (e.g. username=johndoe&exact=true).
    • first (int): Pagination offset (default 0).
    • max (int): Maximum results to return (default 100).
    • enabled (bool): Filter by active status.
cURL Request
curl -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin/realms/gothru/users?username=johndoe&exact=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
Response (200 OK)
[
  {
    "id": "399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d",
    "createdTimestamp": 1710000000000,
    "username": "johndoe",
    "enabled": true,
    "totp": false,
    "emailVerified": true,
    "firstName": "John",
    "lastName": "Doe",
    "email": "johndoe@example.com",
    "attributes": {
      "local_user_id": ["1054"]
    },
    "disableableCredentialTypes": [],
    "requiredActions": [],
    "notBefore": 0,
    "access": {
      "manageGroupMembership": true,
      "view": true,
      "mapRoles": true,
      "impersonate": true,
      "manage": true
    }
  }
]

Get User by ID

  • Method: GET
  • Path: /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user_id}
cURL Request
curl -X GET "http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin/realms/gothru/users/399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"

Update User

  • Method: PUT
  • Path: /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user_id}
  • Success Status: 204 No Content
Request Payload
{
  "firstName": "Jonathan",
  "lastName": "Doe",
  "email": "jonathan.doe@example.com",
  "enabled": true,
  "attributes": {
    "local_user_id": ["1054"],
    "company": ["GoThru LLC"]
  }
}
cURL Request
curl -X PUT "http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin/realms/gothru/users/399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"firstName":"Jonathan","lastName":"Doe"}'

Delete User

  • Method: DELETE
  • Path: /admin/realms/{realm}/users/{user_id}
  • Success Status: 204 No Content
cURL Request
curl -X DELETE "http://127.0.0.1:8180/admin/realms/gothru/users/399eeec3-e18e-4a6a-8b1e-28b497ee359d" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"

Set / Reset User Password

  • Method: PUT

  "value": "NewSecurePassword123!",

}

Tip

If temporary is set to true, the user will be forced to change their password upon their next login.

5. Step-by-Step Code Tutorials

5.1 Node.js / TypeScript Example

Using standard fetch to create a user and assign a role via the Admin REST API.

import { fetch } from 'undici'; // or built-in fetch in Node.js 18+

interface KeycloakConfig {
  baseUrl: string;
  adminRealm: string;
  targetRealm: string;
  adminUser: string;
  adminPass: string;
}

const config: KeycloakConfig = {
  baseUrl: process.env.KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL || 'http://127.0.0.1:8180',
  adminRealm: 'master',
  targetRealm: 'gothru',
  adminUser: process.env.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME || 'admin',
  adminPass: process.env.KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD || 'admin',
};

// 1. Get Admin Access Token
async function getAdminToken(): Promise<string> {
  const tokenUrl = `${config.baseUrl}/realms/${config.adminRealm}/protocol/openid-connect/token`;
  const params = new URLSearchParams({
    client_id: 'admin-cli',
    grant_type: 'password',
    username: config.adminUser,
    password: config.adminPass,
  });

  const res = await fetch(tokenUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
    body: params.toString(),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Failed to obtain admin token: ${res.statusText}`);
  }

  const data = (await res.json()) as { access_token: string };
  return data.access_token;
}

// 2. Create User in GoThru Realm
async function createUser(token: string, user: { username: string; email: string; firstName: string; lastName: string }) {
  const usersUrl = `${config.baseUrl}/admin/realms/${config.targetRealm}/users`;
  const res = await fetch(usersUrl, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      username: user.username,
      email: user.email,
      firstName: user.firstName,
      lastName: user.lastName,
      enabled: true,
      emailVerified: true,
    }),
  });

  if (res.status === 201) {
    const location = res.headers.get('location') || '';
    const userId = location.split('/').pop();
    console.log(`User created successfully with ID: ${userId}`);
    return userId;
  } else if (res.status === 409) {
    console.log('User already exists in Keycloak');
  } else {
    throw new Error(`User creation failed: ${res.status} ${res.statusText}`);
  }
}

// Execute
async function run() {
  const token = await getAdminToken();
  await createUser(token, {
    username: 'developer1',
    email: 'developer1@gothru.co',
    firstName: 'Dev',
    lastName: 'GoThru',
  });
}

run().catch(console.error);

5.2 Go Example

Verifying a Keycloak Access Token via the Userinfo endpoint in a Go backend service (matches the Panorra API pattern).

package main

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"time"
)

type KeycloakUserInfo struct {
	Sub               string `json:"sub"`
	EmailVerified     bool   `json:"email_verified"`
	PreferredUsername string `json:"preferred_username"`
	Email             string `json:"email"`
	Name              string `json:"name"`
	GivenName         string `json:"given_name"`
	FamilyName        string `json:"family_name"`
}

type KeycloakService struct {
	BaseURL    string
	Realm      string
	HTTPClient *http.Client
}

func NewKeycloakService(baseURL, realm string) *KeycloakService {
	return &KeycloakService{
		BaseURL: baseURL,
		Realm:   realm,
		HTTPClient: &http.Client{
			Timeout: 10 * time.Second,
		},
	}
}

func (s *KeycloakService) VerifyAccessToken(accessToken string) (*KeycloakUserInfo, error) {
	if accessToken == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("access token is empty")
	}

	userInfoURL := fmt.Sprintf("%s/realms/%s/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo", s.BaseURL, s.Realm)
	req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", userInfoURL, nil)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+accessToken)
	req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")

	resp, err := s.HTTPClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to call Keycloak: %w", err)
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()

	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusUnauthorized || resp.StatusCode == http.StatusForbidden {
		return nil, errors.New("invalid or expired token")
	}
	if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
		body, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("keycloak returned status %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))
	}

	var info KeycloakUserInfo
	if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&info); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to decode userinfo: %w", err)
	}

	return &info, nil
}

func main() {
	svc := NewKeycloakService("https://gothru-sso.web.id", "gothru")
	user, err := svc.VerifyAccessToken("YOUR_TEST_ACCESS_TOKEN")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Verification error: %v\n", err)
		return
	}
	fmt.Printf("Authenticated GoThru User: %s (%s, sub=%s)\n", user.PreferredUsername, user.Email, user.Sub)
}

5.3 PHP Example

Requesting an Admin Token and resetting a user password (matches the GoThru migration scripts pattern in poc/migrate-users.php).

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

class KeycloakAdminClient
{
    private string $baseUrl;
    private string $realm;
    private ?string $token = null;

    public function __construct(string $baseUrl, string $realm)
    {
        $this->baseUrl = rtrim($baseUrl, '/');
        $this->realm = $realm;
    }

    public function login(string $adminRealm, string $username, string $password): void
    {
        $url = "{$this->baseUrl}/realms/{$adminRealm}/protocol/openid-connect/token";
        $payload = http_build_query([
            'grant_type' => 'password',
            'client_id' => 'admin-cli',
            'username' => $username,
            'password' => $password,
        ]);

        $ch = curl_init($url);
        curl_setopt_array($ch, [
            CURLOPT_POST => true,
            CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => $payload,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => ['Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'],
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 15,
        ]);

        $response = curl_exec($ch);
        $status = (int)curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE);
        curl_close($ch);

        $json = json_decode((string)$response, true);
        if ($status !== 200 || empty($json['access_token'])) {
            throw new RuntimeException("Keycloak login failed with status {$status}");
        }

        $this->token = $json['access_token'];
    }

    public function resetPassword(string $userId, string $newPassword, bool $temporary = false): bool
    {
        $url = "{$this->baseUrl}/admin/realms/{$this->realm}/users/" . rawurlencode($userId) . "/reset-password";
        $payload = json_encode([
            'type' => 'password',
            'value' => $newPassword,
            'temporary' => $temporary,
        ], JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

        $ch = curl_init($url);
        curl_setopt_array($ch, [
            CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST => 'PUT',
            CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS => $payload,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => [
                'Authorization: Bearer ' . $this->token,
                'Content-Type: application/json',
            ],
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 15,
        ]);

        $response = curl_exec($ch);
        $status = (int)curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_RESPONSE_CODE);
        curl_close($ch);

        return $status === 204;
    }
}

5.4 Python Example

Using requests for client credentials authentication and fetching realm users.

import os
import requests

BASE_URL = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8180")
REALM = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_REALM", "gothru")
ADMIN_USER = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USERNAME", "admin")
ADMIN_PASS = os.getenv("KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin")

def get_admin_token() -> str:
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token"
    data = {
        "client_id": "admin-cli",
        "grant_type": "password",
        "username": ADMIN_USER,
        "password": ADMIN_PASS,
    }
    resp = requests.post(url, data=data, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()["access_token"]

def list_users(token: str, max_results: int = 50):
    url = f"{BASE_URL}/admin/realms/{REALM}/users"
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
        "Accept": "application/json",
    }
    params = {"first": 0, "max": max_results}
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    token = get_admin_token()
    users = list_users(token)
    print(f"Retrieved {len(users)} users from realm '{REALM}':")
    for u in users:
        print(f" - {u.get('username')} <{u.get('email')}> [ID: {u.get('id')}]")

6. HTTP Status Codes & Error Handling

HTTP Status Meaning Typical Cause in Keycloak
200 OK Success Request succeeded and body contains data.
201 Created Resource Created User, client, or role created. Look at Location header for ID.
204 No Content Success (No Body) Update, delete, password reset, or role assignment completed.
400 Bad Request Invalid Request Missing required body, invalid JSON, or invalid parameter values.
401 Unauthorized Invalid Authentication Access token expired, missing Bearer token, or invalid admin credentials.
403 Forbidden Permission Denied The authenticated account lacks necessary realm/admin roles (e.g. manage-users).
404 Not Found Resource Missing User ID, Client UUID, or Role Name does not exist.
409 Conflict Duplicate Resource User with username or email already exists.
502 Bad Gateway Network / Proxy Failure Keycloak instance is unreachable or reverse proxy failed.

Common Error Responses

Duplicate User Error (409 Conflict)

{
  "errorMessage": "User exists with same username"
}

Expired Token Error (401 Unauthorized)

{
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "error_description": "Token has expired"
}

7. Security & Best Practices

  1. Never Expose Client Secrets in Frontend:
    • Single Page Applications (Angular, React, Vue) and mobile apps must use public clients with PKCE (S256). Never embed client secrets in client-side code.
  2. Short-Lived Access Tokens:
    • Keep Access Token Lifespan short (e.g., 5 minutes) and use Refresh Tokens to maintain sessions.
  3. Validate JWT Locally When Possible:
    • High-throughput backend APIs should validate tokens locally using JWKS (/certs) with signature and expiry checks rather than hitting /userinfo on every request.
  4. Use sub for User Foreign Keys:
    • Keycloak's sub UUID is immutable. Usernames and emails can be modified by users; always link your local database records to sub.
  5. Use Service Accounts for Machine-to-Machine Integration:
    • Use dedicated client IDs with client_credentials grant rather than sharing admin user credentials.
  6. Paginate List Queries:
    • Always supply first and max query parameters when querying /admin/realms/{realm}/users to prevent performance degradation on large databases (e.g., 55,000+ users).
